system_description.narrative_title: Energy Shock, Bond Stress and Fractured Security in a Tightly Coupled World
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order functions as a single open system driven by overlapping shocks: renewed U.S.–Iran hostilities that threaten Strait of Hormuz flows and lift oil prices, a consequent surge in global bond yields and inflation worries that push central banks toward hawkish policy, and concurrent geopolitical re‑alignments (Russia–Ukraine, U.S.–Venezuela energy deals, China’s outreach) that reshape trade and security linkages. Financial markets, energy logistics, military operations and the technology/AI sphere are tightly coupled so that disruptions in one domain rapidly propagate to others. The system is in flux with high contagion and feedback risks across markets, supply chains and regional security complexes.
system_description.scope: Nation-states, militaries and alliances; international organisations; global energy production, shipping routes (notably the Strait of Hormuz) and commodity markets; international financial markets (sovereign bonds, yields, inflation expectations); major corporations (energy, tech, manufacturing, retail); AI and critical-infrastructure risks; trade and supply chains.
system_description.super_system: The planetary socio-economic-ecological system (global political-economy embedded in Earth’s environmental constraints).

variables.name: US–Iran military escalation
variables.description: The United States and Iran are exchanging strikes and widening military operations across the Middle East, shifting regional security dynamics and alliance postures.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine sustained war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain locked in intensive warfare marked by drone, missile and ground campaigns, with sustained external support altering frontline dynamics and conflict endurance.

variables.name: U.S.–China strategic competition
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting economic and technological primacy across AI, semiconductors, trade and Taiwan-related influence, reshaping global supply chains and governance norms.

variables.name: Global bond market stress
variables.description: Global government bond markets are undergoing a sharp selloff with rising long-term yields as central banks and fiscal trajectories recalibrate, shifting capital flows and financial-stability risks.

variables.name: Energy market realignment
variables.description: Global oil production and access are being reconfigured by new deals, investment shifts and producer coordination, notably including Western engagement in Venezuela and evolving OPEC+ positioning.
